project.name: Royal Match Clone
project.description: A mobile-first match-3 puzzle game built with the PlayCanvas engine (WebGL) for rendering and React for UI. Mirrors the style and core gameplay loop of the mobile hit Royal Match. Features 1000 levels with escalating difficulty: every 3rd level is Hard, every 6th is Super Hard.

style.aesthetic: Bright, clean mobile-first design with a colorful procedural gem aesthetic. Rich transition animation and rendered particle VFX remain future presentation work.
style.engine: PlayCanvas engine (npm: playcanvas) for WebGL rendering

layer.name: engine
layer.purpose: PlayCanvas PC.Application lifecycle, scene setup, entity management, camera, lighting, VFX. Pure bridge between logic state and WebGL rendering.

layer.name: game
layer.purpose: Framework-agnostic match-3 core: board, grid, pieces, match finding, drop simulation, scoring, goals, input, state machine. No React or PlayCanvas imports here.

layer.name: ui
layer.purpose: React components: screens, HUD, menus, level select, modals. Uses hooks to subscribe to game state.

layer.name: data
layer.purpose: Static game data: piece types, colors, goals, boosts, board configs, level metadata.

layer.name: levels
layer.purpose: Level data: generator, difficulty rules, and 1000 generated level JSON files split into folders of 100.

layer.name: utils
layer.purpose: Shared utilities, math helpers, RNG (deterministic), debounce, deep clone, etc.

architecture.dataFlow: 1. LevelGenerator produces a LevelData JSON (deterministic seed). 2. LevelLoader reads JSON into the GameState. 3. Board logic processes swaps/matches/drops. 4. Engine renders the Board state as PlayCanvas entities. 5. UI subscribes to GameState (Zustand) and re-renders HUD. 6. Input (mouse/touch) flows: React input capture -> GameManager -> Board.

levelSystem.levelFormat: Each level is a JSON file: src/levels/levels/{range}/level-{NNNN}.json Schema (validated by Zod schema in src/levels/LevelData.ts):
levelSystem.levelSchema: levelNumber (integer 1-1000) difficulty (enum: EASY | NORMAL | HARD | SUPER_HARD) title (string) description (string) grid { cols, rows } moveLimit (integer) scoreStar1 (integer, 1-star threshold) scoreStar2 (integer, 2-star threshold) scoreStar3 (integer, 3-star threshold) objectives (array of objective objects) boardLayout (2D array of cell definitions: EMPTY | BLOCKED | OBSTACLE_{type} | GEM_{color}) preplacedSpecials (array, optional special pieces at start) rewards { coins, stars, unlocks }

type.desc: Collect N gems of a specific color
Not emitted until item entities are implemented
Not emitted until drop objects are implemented

milestone.name: Match-3 core logic (Board, Grid, Piece, MatchFinder)
React UI: splash, main menu, level select

notes.note: This project uses deterministic RNG (seedrandom-style) so any level is reproducible. DO NOT use Math.random() in the level generator or board logic; use src/utils/rng.ts (deterministic).
Each GameScreen owns one PlayCanvas application. Gem and obstacle entities are reused through the renderer's typed pools; keep allocation outside hot render loops.
All 1000 level files are generated by running "npm run generate:levels" which executes scripts/generate-levels.ts. The script is deterministic.
Runtime UI flow: SPLASH -> MAIN_MENU -> LEVEL_SELECT -> GAME -> LEVEL_COMPLETE.
The shop, rendered particles, and interpolated animation queue are not runtime features. Do not present their placeholder files as complete.
